newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian sowing may meet target in good weather.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian sowing may meet target in good weather.

text.p: Bulgaria has sown 81 percent of the planned acreage for wheat and barley so far and concerns about autumn sowing are receding, an agriculture ministry official said on Wednesday.
"Wheat sowings have covered some 1.04 million hectares, while some 250,000 hectares have been sown with barley so far," ministry's spokeswoman Roza Trichkova told Reuters.
Trichkova said good weather had prolonged the sowing period, which was initially expected to end around November 5.
"If the weather remains favourable and sowing proceeds at the same pace, Bulgaria is expected to sow the planned 1.6 million hectares of wheat and barley," she said.
Bulgaria's parliament passed a bill last month to unblock farmers' funds from banks placed in receivership by the central bank and to provide incentives for the farmers.
Under the bill, the purchase prices of wheat, maize and barley from the 1996-97 harvest will be not less than 80 percent of the international price.
Low domestic prices encouraged high exports last year, which combined with a poor harvest last summer to produce an acute grain shortage.

Last year Bulgaria sowed one million ha with wheat and 270,000 ha with barley. But some analysts say that as sown acreage is not much higher this autumn, the country could face another grain shortage next year. -- Galina Sabeva, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
